subject.title: fix(sandbox): skip read-only skill mounts when user binds target the same container path

question: Should protected read-only skill destinations always override user binds, including binds enabled through the reserved-target break-glass setting?
rationale: Both outcomes are defensible but materially different: the PR preserves skill immutability by ignoring explicit configuration, while honoring the bind would weaken the protected mount boundary; repository behavior alone cannot establish the intended permanent contract.

options.title: Keep protected mounts authoritative
options.body: Accept the PR's precedence rule, retain operator warnings, and require the proof script to return nonzero on any failed assertion.

options.title: Reject conflicts during validation
options.body: Replace runtime filtering with an actionable configuration error that names the conflicting destination before Docker creation.

options.title: Honor break-glass binds
options.body: Let explicitly allowed user binds win and document that this can weaken read-only skill protection.

recommendation.title: Keep protected mounts authoritative
recommendation.body: Accept the PR's precedence rule, retain operator warnings, and require the proof script to return nonzero on any failed assertion.

likelyOwner.reason: The timeline routed this security and compatibility decision to steipete, and the choice sets a core sandbox policy rather than a mechanical implementation detail.
